# Consumer Healthcare Support

`customer_support.model.b2c.healthcare_consumer` · vertical · parent `customer_support.model.b2c`

> Supporting patients and members of a consumer health service — telehealth, pharmacy delivery, diagnostics, insurance member services, health apps. The defining constraint is that the boundary between support and clinical advice is legally sharp and conversationally invisible. A patient describing symptoms to explain why their order matters has just moved the conversation somewhere an agent is not licensed to go, and the correct move — acknowledge, do not interpret, route to a clinician — has to survive the pull of an obviously distressed person asking a reasonable question. This is the single most important thing to encode about the vertical. The second fact is that delay has clinical consequence. A late prescription, a delayed result or a failed appointment booking is not a service inconvenience but a health event, and severity therefore tracks clinical risk rather than system impact. A partial outage of a repeat- prescription path outranks a total outage of almost anything else. Third, privacy is a hard control rather than a preference. Health data attracts the strictest handling obligations of any vertical in this library: who may see a record, what may be written in a ticket, what may be sent by email, and who may speak on a patient's behalf are all constrained by law rather than by policy. Family members calling about a relative are the routine case and the routine refusal. The error carried in from ecommerce is speed-first triage. Answering fast and reassuringly is usually correct and here is sometimes the harm.


## Characteristics

|  |  |
|---|---|
| requester | a patient or member, frequently anxious and sometimes acutely unwell, occasionally a family member or carer with no authority to receive anything |
| typical_resolution_hours | 4 |
| volume_shape | steady with seasonal peaks (respiratory season, renewals, policy periods) and sharp spikes on any interruption to a prescription or results pathway |
| staffing_model | non-clinical agents with a hard, fast handoff to licensed clinicians; separate pharmacy and claims paths; strict role-based access to records |
| coverage | extended hours at minimum, 24x7 wherever a prescription, results or urgent-care pathway exists |
| automation_level | high on logistics, booking and billing intents; hard-blocked on anything symptom-adjacent, where an automated answer is both a clinical risk and a regulatory breach |
| notes | The safest default is that an agent may describe process and never interpret content. "Your result is available and here is how to discuss it" is support; anything about what the result means is not.  |

## Extends `customer_support.obj.core.ticket`

Requires `severity`, `priority`, `intent_ref`


> Severity here reads clinical risk rather than system impact, which inverts the usual relationship with blast radius: a single patient unable to obtain a repeat prescription outranks a cosmetic fault affecting everyone. Intent must be able to flag symptom-adjacent contacts before an agent begins composing.


## Extends `customer_support.obj.core.requester`

Requires `affected_user_ref`, `is_admin`, `accessibility_needs`


> The person contacting is frequently not the patient — a carer, a parent, a family member — and whether they may lawfully receive anything is a verification question that precedes every substantive reply. This is the object where the writer-is-not-the-sufferer problem stops being a reproduction nuisance and becomes a legal control.


## Extends `customer_support.obj.core.escalation`

Requires `origin`, `reason_category`, `escalation_owner_ref`, `requested_at`


> A clinical handoff is an exit from the support process into a licensed function, not a transfer to a more senior agent. Recording the reason category and the timestamp is what makes the boundary auditable, and auditability is the point.


## Extends `customer_support.obj.core.knowledge_article`

Requires `audience`, `accuracy_state`, `verified_against_version`


> Published health content carries obligations that ordinary support content does not, and a stale article here can cause harm rather than inconvenience. Audience matters more than anywhere else in the library: internal guidance for agents and patient-facing content are different artefacts with different approval paths, and conflating them is the failure.

> Jurisdictional detail is deliberately absent — which privacy regime, which licensure rules, which retention obligations — because those belong in a tenant's organisation brain rather than in the profession's knowledge. What generalises is the shape: a hard clinical boundary non-clinical agents must not cross, delay as clinical risk, third-party callers as the routine case, and support output as a regulated record.
